prompt:
Use case: style-transfer / map redesign.
Create the NEXT ITERATION of the western village arena in image 1, following the producer's confirmed feedback: streets, central square AND BUILDING INTERIORS need to be much larger in proportion to characters; environment should be calmer to keep combat readable. One whole-map 16:10 overhead concept, exactly FOUR small characters.

Image 1 is the previous village COMPOSITION, keep its western identity and approximate zoning. Geometry is free to change. Image 2 is the preferred soft-shaded pixel-art rendering reference, NOT a room-size template. Retain its pleasant gentle shaded volumes, but reduce the environment's visual intensity.

CRITICAL CHANGE 1 — SCALE AND USABLE SPACE:
Make the four characters approximately HALF THEIR DISPLAYED HEIGHT in image 1. On an approximately 1600 x 1000 full-map image, each entire person should be about 35 to 42 pixels high, not 70 to 90 pixels high. They must remain crisp and recognizable. Scale ALL TABLES, CHAIRS, BARRELS, DOORS, SHELVES, CRATES and tile units consistently with that human scale. Do not just shrink the characters while leaving gigantic chairs.
The accessible buildings occupy similar or slightly larger image footprints but are substantially roomier in WORLD proportions: each saloon/shop interior should be at least 10 to 14 character heights across, with large contiguous open floor. Furniture is clustered only along useful room edges; keep 3 modest card tables in the saloon, not more, and no extra dense decoration. Each table should be comparable in width to one character's hat, not 3 times wider.
Push the saloon left and general store right toward the sides. Make the CENTRAL SQUARE genuinely generous, roughly 30 percent of image width across the middle, not a narrow corridor between opposing doors. The main street remains broad as it runs north-south. Main movement corridors at least 6 to 8 sombrero widths; secondary outdoor routes 3 to 4 character widths. Doorways at least 2 character widths. These are VISUAL STUDY proportions, not captions or technical overlays.
The redesign must clearly look like space where four people can run, dodge, cross and flank. Add usable floor inside and outside, not more buildings or props to fill every gap. Keep clear ground immediately inside and outside all main entrances.

CRITICAL CHANGE 2 — READABILITY HIERARCHY:
The environment is pleasant, readable and recognizable but SIGNIFICANTLY LESS CONTRASTY than image 1. Crisp pixel-art edges are retained; DO NOT blur or defocus anything. Achieve calm through lower saturation and closer tones, not blur or fog.
Quiet pale ochre sand with almost no speckle; very subtle wheel tracks only. Muted blue-gray interior floor with barely visible grout. NO strong dark tile grid. Walls and furniture outlined in medium warm brown, never heavy near-black. Contact shadows on environment are short, restrained midtones, not thick black borders. Reduce roof/ridge striping, wood grain, pebble texture, lantern highlights and tiny trim. Concentrate small material details against the outer walls, loading areas and closed houses. Do not put decorative stuff on the square.
Characters get the strongest dark outlines and richest localized colors: golden hat/olive crown, charcoal hat/red scarf/violet sleeves, blue scarf/brown hat, ochre outfit/pale hat. The single green tequila bottle also gets a clear small silhouette. Keep warm soft shading and volume inside objects; do not convert everything to harsh flat vector shapes or make the whole picture blurry/pale.

KEEP THE APPROVED WESTERN TOWN STRUCTURE:
Saloon on the left, open roof, blue-gray floor, L-shaped bar against upper-left inner area, three small card tables/chairs along room margins, burgundy couch/rug by lower wall. Lots of continuous central floor, two broad routes through its main and rear openings.
General store on the right, open roof, enlarged blue-gray interior; weighing counter and goods shelves near its back/side walls, a few sacks/produce boxes in a loading corner. No gambling tables or second saloon. Wide open interior floor and front/back connections.
Fenced yard upper-right, trough, modest storage corner, clear gate openings.
Tool/storage shed lower-left, plank floor, tools and crate/barrel storage along edges, clear working floor.
Closed dwellings with roofs and small porches stay peripheral, do not add extra houses. Use them, partial fences, courtyard walls and dry rocks to suggest a village that continues beyond north and south. No continuous enclosing fortress wall.
Keep two broad continuous rear/side circulation loops. Main street and square should be the dominant open shared area. Functional placement of cover and storage at edges; no randomly scattered isolated crates in the combat space. No new large central landmark obstructing combat.

EXACTLY FOUR FIGURES, HALF THE PREVIOUS DISPLAYED HEIGHT:
Poncho is on clear floor INSIDE the enlarged saloon near the lower/central open area, visibly small relative to the room. Broad straw-gold sombrero with raised olive crown; brown weighted cloth hangs to the floor and covers feet; short attached shadow, no floating.
Garcia stands on the right half of the central square. Charcoal wide-brim hat with tiny gold star, violet sleeves, red neckerchief, planted boots.
Brown cowboy-hat / BLUE SCARF placeholder stands on the upper side street between the saloon's rear and the yard approach.
Pale broad hat / charcoal crown / OCHRE CLOTHING placeholder stands on clear floor INSIDE the shop, well away from furniture and wall shadows.
All have the same physical scale and distinctive reference identities, held small weapons, neutral grounded poses. No NPCs, duplicates, animals or extra portraits.
Exactly one small green tequila bottle on the central square, no halo, rings or markers.

CAMERA AND STYLE:
Entire map in one orthographic top-down 2D game view, small visible frontal wall/furniture faces, no isometric angle, no vanishing-point perspective, no 3D aerial painting. Both open-roof buildings fully visible. Soft-shaded chunky pixel art with intentional color clusters and stair-step silhouettes; no blurry resampling or photo detail. The relative scale change and quiet environment should be immediately obvious against image 1.
No text, no labels, signs, HUD, bars, player numbers, circles, diamonds, legend, arrows, paths drawn as diagram lines, inset or border. No effects, firing, dust or speed lines in this base image. This is a new art-direction mockup, not an engine screenshot or measured collision map.
